rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5173, ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD AS A SEPARATE AND DISTINCT SERVICE AND ATTACHING THE SAME TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The urgent need to separate and professionalize the PCG has time and again been brought to fore by compelling events and disasters that continue to plague the country's maritime industry. Costly accidents at sea with thousands of lives lost, unabated environmental degradation, destruction of maritime resources, deadly red tide, and the recent fishkills at Manila Bay and Laguna Lake have made the separation of the Philippine coast Guard relevant and imperative. "The Philippine coast guard Law of 1996" Proposes to SEPARATE the PCG from the Philippine Navy and attach it to the DOTC.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 1997-12-03

rows.abstract: Rationale: It is noted that many cases involving bouncing checks now clogged the docket of our courts. rows.abstract: Rationale: The advent of RA 7659 amending RA 6425, otherwise known as Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972 as amended, was a welcome haven to drug users and drug traffickers. Instead of giving more teeth and spirit to the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972 as amended, it only created a monster with no fangs and spine!!! The floodgates of drug trafficking is again widely-opened. Why? First, RA 6425 was given retroactive effect. Second, the quantity of dangerous drugs involved determines the basis of the penlatyimposable. Third, modifying circumstances are noe considered in imposing penalty for the violation of RA 6425 to the extent of lowering imposable penalty be lower than prision correccional.

rows.abstract: States that a NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM shall be established in the country to be administered by the National Statistics Office. rows.abstract: Rationale: The State is duty bound under the Constitution to promote and protect our children's physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual and social well-being so that they will be fully prepared when they assume their responsibility in shaping our country's future. > By giving them the proper environment they need, these chidlren will make this nation truly great. rows.author: A102
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING FURTHER THE RIGHTS OF THE PARTIES UNDER VOLUNTARY ARBITRATION, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 262-A OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: "Recent developments tend to erode the integrity of voluntary arbitration as an equitable, expeditious and inexpensive mode of settling labor disputes." Seeks to RESTORE the confidence once enjoyed by voluntary arbitration as the primarymode of albor dsipute resolution by: (1) restating tht the decision/award of the voluntary arbitrator is final and executory and thus no motion for consideration may be entertained by the voluntary arbitrator; (2) clarifying that, unless otherwise ordered by the Court, the aspect of the decision/award of the voluntary arbitrator ordering reinstatement shall not be stayed by the mere filing of a petition for a certiorari; and (3) requiring the posting of a supersedeas bond equivalent to the monettary award in the decision/award as a jurisdictional prerequisite in filing a certiorari petition seeking the review of said decision/award.
rows.status: Substituted by HB09333
